falsification.issue_1: V1 can mechanically accept an arbitrary relation R_Q because the certificate has no load-bearing receipt proving that each related Brain quotient state is noninferior to its target state on the complete acceptance-relevant material order.
falsification.constructive_counterexample: Label T1 as target terminal quality 1 and B1 as Brain terminal quality 0, declare relation [[T0,B0],[T1,B1]], provide graph-complete edges and the existing Boolean/receipt flags. V1 has no acceptance values or relation-soundness receipt to distinguish this from a valid noninferior relation, so graph PASS does not entail terminal noninferiority.
falsification.issue_2: V1 treats scope_authority_invariant=true on each Brain macroedge as a naked self-asserted Boolean rather than requiring an independent scope-complete semantic receipt.
falsification.consequence: V1 is admissible only as a graph-mechanics kernel. It is not sufficient to verify the theorem premises needed for terminal noninferiority and must not receive activation or acceptance credit as a complete quotient-simulation verifier.

repair.role: V2 converts the previously implicit semantic assumptions into explicit content-addressed obligations. It still does not independently verify the bytes of those receipts; that remains a separate promotion gate.
